summary: Backend-only testing of new image upload/download feature (Emergent Managed Object Storage). All 11 new tests + 45 regression tests PASS (56/56, 13.71s). Verified: (1) POST /api/upload admin flow returns 200 with correct {path, url, relative_url, size} shape; path matches 'avr-organics/uploads/{user_id}/{uuid}.{ext}'. (2) Auth gating: no token -> 401, non-admin -> 403, admin -> 200. (3) Validation: empty body -> 400, non-image content-type (application/pdf) -> 400, >8MB -> 413. (4) GET /api/files/{path}?token=<public_token> works unauth and returns correct content-type (image/png) and identical bytes. (5) Bearer session (any logged-in user) also authorizes download. (6) Public access when product.image references the path works without any auth. (7) No token + no auth + path not referenced by any product -> 401. (8) Unknown path -> 404. REGRESSION: All existing admin product CRUD, categories CRUD, merchant/callmebot admin, admin orders list+status, orders/create for upi and razorpay all PASS.

minor.issue: Public-access check uses regex match on products.image containing full_path. Safe here (uuid filename) but theoretically a prefix of one upload's path could appear in an unrelated product's image URL. Low risk; consider exact match on the ?token query substring instead.

ext fallback is 'bin' for unknown image/* subtypes (e.g. image/svg+xml). Download will still succeed because content_type is persisted, but the stored filename extension can mislead CDNs/browsers that sniff by extension.
Pre-existing: does not cascade on products (non-blocking, flagged in iter 4).

action_items: No action required — image upload/download feature is working as specified. All 7 required scenarios pass.

Optional (non-blocking): tighten public-access check in GET /api/files/{path} by matching on the token-bearing URL substring rather than regex on full_path to prevent theoretical substring collisions.
Optional (non-blocking): add explicit ext mapping for 'image/svg+xml' or reject it since SVGs can contain scripts.
critical_code_review_comments: Upload path layout correctly namespaces by APP_NAME ('avr-organics') and owner user_id — safe multi-tenant.
Three-tier authorization in /api/files/{path} (public_token, Bearer session, product.image reference) matches the review spec exactly.
require_admin() layered on get_current_user() produces correct 401-before-403 ordering, verified end-to-end.
File size check (8MB) happens AFTER read() — a very large upload still buffers into memory before 413. Fine for 8MB cap; worth noting if cap is raised.

_init_storage() stale-key re-init pattern inside _put_object is only applied to the PUT path, not to _get_object — if download gets a 503 stale-key response once, it will surface as 500 to clients. Minor; consider mirroring the re-init-once pattern for GET.
seed_data_creation: Reused session-scoped seeded_user + seeded_admin fixtures (conftest.py). Created a 1x1 red PNG (~70 bytes) in-memory for all upload tests to stay well under storage quota. All uploads rows deleted + any TEST_-prefixed products cleaned in fixture teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Env var is EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (not EXPO_BACKEND_URL). Run: `set -a && . /app/frontend/.env && set +a && pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v`. Storage credit is finite — keep upload payloads tiny (<1KB PNG). Admin OAuth bypassed by seeding users + user_sessions directly in Mongo (herbal_bloom). Upload path pattern is avr-organics/uploads/{user_id}/{uuid}.{ext} — do not assume a fixed extension; tests should use .startswith/endswith. Downloads also work with any logged-in Bearer, not just admin.
rca_of_issue: Not applicable — this iteration validates a NEW FEATURE (not a bug fix). The user-reported bug ('I am not able to view Pictures, even after posting the Image links') is addressed by (a) replacing the broken external URL dependency with direct device-gallery upload via /api/upload, (b) adding inline onError preview in Product Editor, and (c) serving uploaded images from /api/files/{path} with a three-tier access model (per-file public_token, Bearer session, or product.image reference for catalog browsing). Backend contract fully exercised and green.
